what: Add hooks/lib/safe-write.js: lstat symlink refusal, temp file in resolved dir, O_EXCL plus O_NOFOLLOW (0 on win32) mode 0600, rename; win32 ownership check = tmpdir/homedir containment. title: hush: log template mining lossless rung
why: Dupe-collapse only merges identical consecutive lines; real logs repeat shapes with varying IDs and timestamps. A lossless template collapse compounds the strongest domain before any lossy cap.
what: collapseTemplates() after dupe collapse, before capLines: same token count, half of positions identical, 2+ constant anchor tokens, run of 5+ collapses to first line + hush-hook marker with count. SIGNAL_RE lines never join and always break runs. Replay-validate on fixtures first; ship only if replay shows real gains. Spec 5, docs/hush/research/hush-competitor-intel-2026-07-13.md.
notes: SHIPPED. collapseTemplates() added in hush/hooks/compress-tool-output.js: tokenize on /\s+/, two lines share a template iff same token count, >=50% positions token-identical, >=2 anchor tokens (len>=3, no digits) among those identical positions; comparison is always against the run anchor (run's first line), not chained pairwise. SIGNAL_RE lines never join/never start a run and flush any in-progress run. Runs >= TEMPLATE_MIN_RUN=5 (env HUSH_TEMPLATE_MIN_RUN) collapse to first line verbatim + '[hush hook: N similar lines collapsed (same shape, varying values)]' where N=runLen-1. Inserted in compress() between dedupeConsecutive and capLines; skipped when enumerate=true (matches the existing sidecar carve-out philosophy: a completeness request must see every item, so collapsing would contradict its no-omission promise) or HUSH_TEMPLATE=off. Exported from the module and documented in README settings table. REPLAY GATE (required numbers): log-triage/logs/app.log (719-line redis outage log, rotating api/worker-1/worker-2/scheduler endpoints) = 0% incremental reduction beyond dedupeConsecutive (57326->57326 chars) - the algorithm correctly refuses to merge lines whose service+path genuinely differ each step, no false positives. incident-pool-leak/logs/worker.log = 0% (21057->21057 chars), same rotating-shape reason. incident-pool-leak/logs/app.log = 4.16% incremental (23407->22433 chars post-dedupe basis). noisy-build (build.js stdout, ~900 compile lines) = 77.20% incremental reduction (28320->6457 chars post-dedupe basis) - this is the domain Spec 5 targeted (uniform compile-line noise) and the gain is large, not trivial. Gate reads 'trivial on both fixtures' as the drop condition; since the required noisy-build fixture shows a massive, non-trivial gain, SHIP is correct per the gate as written, even though log-triage app.log (its access-log shape rotates 3 distinct endpoints every line, never producing 5 consecutive identical-shaped lines) shows none. Manually verified no false merges: all 4 WARN/ERROR signal lines in noisy-build survive verbatim post-collapse. 8 new unit tests added (collapseTemplates describe block): same-shape run collapse, signal-line non-merge, signal breaks an in-progress run, interleaved non-matching line breaks a run, run of 4 untouched, idempotence, exact marker text, HUSH_TEMPLATE=off passthrough. Had to touch 3 pre-existing tests whose synthetic fixtures (unrelated to templates) coincidentally satisfied the template-share rule and started collapsing under the new pipeline step, invalidating their capLines/sidecar-cap assertions: pinned HUSH_TEMPLATE=off for those specific calls (env arg on runHook, or direct process.env toggle for in-process compress() calls) rather than reworking their fixtures. Final: node --test tests/*.test.js = 196/196 pass (188 baseline + 8 new), exit 0. Spec-vs-reality: Spec 5's doc-cited line numbers for compress-tool-output.js were stale (file has grown since); re-located all anchors by symbol name as instructed, no other mismatches found.

title: Trio probe: shell wrapper vs dep-guard
why: Under bypassPermissions (the benchmark environment) hush rewrites shell commands via updatedInput; whether razor's dep-guard still parses a wrapped npm install is untested - the trio benchmark had no install-bait.
what: Zero-API-cost probe: determine whether parallel PreToolUse hooks see original or chained tool_input (scripted settings.json + sentinel command). If chained: generic PowerShell block unwrap + pipe-tail strip in dep-guard parseSegment (shell syntax handling, not sibling detection). Spec R3.
notes: Empirically confirmed live (headless claude -p probe, 2 real plugins loaded via --plugin-dir, hush preserve-exit-code.js + a throwaway sentinel plugin on the same PreToolUse Bash|PowerShell matcher): PreToolUse hooks from separate plugins do NOT chain. The sentinel captured the models ORIGINAL npm install left-pad-probe-xyz tool_input verbatim, never hushs & { ... } | Out-String rewrite, even though a direct stdin invocation of hushs script with the same payload + HUSH_WRAP=1 confirmed it does produce that rewrite. Claude Code invokes every matching hook against the same original tool_call payload and merges decisions/updatedInput afterward (fan-out-then-merge, not a pipeline). Consequence: razor dep-guard.js never receives a hush-wrapped command in practice, so the PowerShell & {}-unwrap fix proposed in Spec R3 is unnecessary - added a one comment note at dep-guard.js above parseInstallCommand instead of changing parsing logic. Correction to the research docs Part 3 fact 16: the transcripts tool_use.input preserves the MODELS original command text, not the post-rewrite executed one (verified directly in stream-json output). No real npm install ever ran (sentinel denied the call before execution; separately verified with a benign echo command that execution proceeds normally when nothing denies). razor bumped to 0.3.13-alpha (doc-only, no behavior change) since marketplace.json requires version+sha to move together with any submodule pointer bump - CHANGELOG entry added. title: probe: TaskCompleted hook contract

what: Headless probe per the 0.21.0 TaskCreated method: --settings logging+blocking hook, claude -p haiku driver creates a task then completes it; record the accepted decision:block JSON shape, whether additionalContext is delivered, and whether the harness retries completion after a block. notes:

(1) Block shape: TaskCompleted accepts the SAME top-level {"decision":"block","reason":"..."} as Stop/SubagentStop -- no separate envelope, no need for the exit-code-2 fallback. probe-block: close the roadmap entry first"} -- but the haiku driver's own final-message prose mischaracterized this as a successful completion despite quoting the reason verbatim, so M1's block-reason text needs to be unambiguous enough to make the model act (retry the close) rather than paraphrase the block away. title: hush: sidecar-follow eval never exercises the follow path
why: Tier-3 run: both arms passed sidecar-follow trivially by grepping the fixture log instead of Reading it - hush decisions show passthrough only, no sidecar fired, so the census-to-follow-read behavior the eval exists to measure was never engaged.

notes: Confirmed root cause: fixture (703-line log) clears SIDECAR_MIN_CHARS, but the old prompt ("tell me exactly which test(s) failed, by name") handed the model an obvious grep target. Grep is NOT in compress-tool-output.js's hooks.json matcher (only Bash|PowerShell|Read|mcp__...), so a single Grep for FAIL/✗ pulled both failing test names straight off the raw fixture file in one small call, never touching hush at all (tier3 hush run: toolCalls=2, debugManifest byAction={passthrough:1}, no sidecar entry ever fired). title: Multi-slice benchmark fixture to measure parallel Fable orchestration
why: The fableorch1 probe (tag fableorch1, benchmarks/foreman/experiments/handoff) covered only single-slice tasks, where orchestration tied direct Fable on correctness and cost at 2x wall clock; foreman 0.40.0-alpha ships the Fable-orchestrator option scoped to tasks with 2+ Run:/Expected: checks, and no harness fixture exercises that shape
what: Build a fixture in benchmarks/foreman/experiments/handoff/fixtures with 2-3 independent planted bugs across disjoint modules, each with its own verification check; reuse the fableorch arm (agents:true, agents/implementer.md sonnet pin, mainEdits/subagentDispatches metrics) vs foreman arm on --model fable, 4 reps, one interleaved batch; measure wall clock (parallel dispatch is the hypothesized win), correctness, cost, orchestration compliance
notes: Fixture built (3 disjoint bugs, own test file + check each), then run: foreman vs fableorch, --model fable, 4 reps, tag multislice1. Result: both 100% correct/tests-pass, 0 violations. fableorch cost MORE (0.9089 vs 0.7182 mean, +26%) and took LONGER wall clock (55s vs 26s mean, ~2.1x). CORRECTED after reading the raw transcripts (not just turn counts): all 4/4 reps DID dispatch the 3 implementer subagents in parallel (all three Task calls fired back-to-back before any subagent result came back, confirmed by interleaved sub-agent events in the event stream) -- so the disjoint-files exception WAS exploited every time, contrary to what an earlier turn-count-only read of this data concluded. The real cost/time driver is a coordination tax: the orchestrator reads all 3 files and runs the test suite itself BEFORE dispatching (reps 1/3/4; rep2 skipped most of this and was both fastest and cheapest of the fableorch reps), then re-reads the changed files and re-runs tests itself AFTER the subagents report back -- i.e. the work gets read and verified twice (once per subagent, once by the orchestrator) even though the fixes themselves parallelize fine. Conclusion: parallel dispatch works as designed on disjoint files, but the orchestrator role still doubles up on the read/verify legwork, which is what erases the wall-clock and cost win, not sequential dispatch. Full report: results/multislice1/report.md (private, gitignored); raw transcripts back this analysis, not just the aggregate table. FOLLOW-UP tag multislice2 (2026-07-23): re-ran against the bullet-trimmed foremanbullets/fableorchbullets arms -- the shape a REAL confirmed-fable-orchestrator craft-prompt call assembles today (read/run-first task_rules bullets dropped per the fable targetModel rule), not the frozen bullet-carrying foreman arm the first pass reused from fableorch1. Result: the gap did not narrow, it widened in relative terms -- fableorchbullets cost +90.8% over foremanbullets (0.7288 vs 0.3820 mean) and took ~2.4x the wall clock (55s vs 23s), vs +26%/2.1x on the untrimmed pair. Direct fable got much cheaper from the trim (0.7182->0.3820, -47%) but the orchestrator barely moved (0.9089->0.7288, -20%). Transcripts confirm why: with or without the bullets, the orchestrator still reads all 3 files itself before dispatching and re-reads + re-runs tests itself after every subagent returns -- driven by the <orchestration> block's own mandatory review step and truth_grounding, not by task_rules micro-steps. CONFIRMED, not a benchmark artifact: the coordination tax is inherent to the orchestrator role on this shape, and using the actually-shipped today prompt only makes the option look worse, not better. Report: results/multislice2/report.md. FOLLOW-UP tag multislice3 (2026-07-23): one interleaved batch, 3 arms x 4 reps, isolating the mandatory-review variable specifically -- foremanbullets (baseline), fableorchbullets (shipped orchestration, WITH mandatory review), fableorchnoreview (same orchestration block minus the review-before-accepting instruction, trusting each subagent's own reported pass/fail; the harness's own scoreRun() independently re-verifies regardless, so ground truth is unaffected). Means: foremanbullets 0.3822/24s, fableorchbullets 0.6893/53s (+80% cost, ~2.2x wall), fableorchnoreview 0.5209/42s (+36% cost, ~1.75x wall). Dropping the review step recovers roughly HALF the orchestration overhead vs baseline -- but a real +36% cost and 1.75x wall-clock penalty survives even when the orchestrator fully trusts its subagents. Transcripts confirm clean isolation: fableorchnoreview still does the upfront own-reads before dispatching (truth_grounding-driven, independent of the orchestration block) but has NO post-dispatch re-read/re-test step, unlike fableorchbullets. Conclusion: the coordination tax splits roughly in half between (1) the mandatory review-before-accepting step and (2) inherent multi-agent overhead (per-subagent context/read/edit/ test cycles cost more in aggregate than one session doing the same work inline) -- neither of which is a benchmark artifact. Three full probes (fableorch1, multislice1/2/3) now agree: no measured shape shows a Fable-orchestrator win on cost or wall clock. Report: results/multislice3/report.md.

title: foreman: three durable guardrails for the handoff prompt
why: truth_grounding tells the session to trust reality over the prompt, but the prompt also prescribes an approach — and nothing says which authority wins when reality contradicts the prescription rather than the facts. Two adjacent holes: nothing forbids inventing an API the prompt claimed exists, and the iterate-until-it-passes verification line has no stop condition.
what: Add three short rules to prompt-template.md. (1) Precedence, inside truth_grounding: facts are hypotheses, the chosen approach is a decision — if the codebase makes it unworkable, stop and report, do not substitute. (2) No-inventing-API, near relevant_files: if a named symbol or fallback path does not exist as described, stop and report, do not create it. (3) A failure ceiling on the verification block: after two failed fix iterations, stop and report — do not widen the change to make tests pass. title: hush failures: preserve native failure semantics and provide recoverable digests
why: Failure compression can hide diagnostic context and change execution semantics, making debugging harder precisely when trust matters most.
what: Keep command execution native by default, classify failures with one shared contract, preserve the exit code and signal, and show the first causal error plus the final summary and rerun guidance. Store the complete failure output through the recovery manifest and fall back to original output if recovery cannot be guaranteed.
notes:
Derived from docs/hush/research/hush-product-contract-and-remediation-2026-07-27.md.

(2) Signal handling is new: bash reports signal death as exit 128+N; PowerShell has no usable signal channel - surface code+signal where derivable, document the PowerShell limit. (3) Silently-wrong wrapper case: trailing ( exit 5 ) subshell records 0 - pin with a test and a README caveat per decision 5; set -e/exit/trap fail closed (test those too). (4) One-shared-contract targets FAILURE_RE vs SIGNAL_RE divergence (case-sensitive fail detection misses lowercase error TS; Build failed with exit code 1 is fail=false/signal=true) - one classifier decides failed-ness for cap selection; failure digest = first causal error + final summary + rerun guidance. (5) Store complete failure output via the recovery manifest: extend maybeSidecar coverage to failing outputs beyond the 15-28KB window; deliver/recoveryGap already enforce drop-on-no-recovery. Boundary vs 167: 166 owns the failure path only; template/search recovery is 167. hooks.json only if the matcher changes. Pre-Wave-C line refs are stale - re-locate.

title: hush transforms: make template and search elision explicitly recoverable
why: Template collapse and search-result summarization intentionally remove detail but do not consistently prove how a user can retrieve the omitted content.
what: Declare the exact invariants for template and search transformations, retain source paths and match coordinates, persist omitted content when the source is not sufficient, and expose a stable retrieval instruction. title: hush architecture: separate Core runtime from Quiet behavior
why: Automatic output handling and intentionally silent interaction are different product choices; coupling them makes defaults, safety, and adoption harder to reason about.
what: Implement the recorded product boundary so Core transforms and recovery can run without Quiet narration constraints, while Quiet remains an explicit capability with its own activation and disable behavior. Update manifests, hooks, settings, and conformance tests so each mode can be installed, enabled, disabled, and evaluated independently.
notes:
Derived from docs/hush/research/hush-product-contract-and-remediation-2026-07-27.md.
2026-07-29 2026-07-29 Wave E dispatch (SS4 carries NO note for 169, so this note IS the dispatch spec; built from SS5 decisions 1/1a/3/4, docs/foreman/tasks/161.md, and a fresh orchestrator read of hooks/, README.md, plugin.json, tests/). (1) Surface assignment, settled - do not re-litigate: CORE = hooks/compress-tool-output.js, hooks/preserve-exit-code.js, hooks/precompact-summary.js, hooks/postcompact-rearm.js, hooks/session-end-cleanup.js, hooks/lib/* (transform-manifest, sidecar-store, safe-write, transcript), skills/hush-stats. QUIET = hooks/silence-nudge.js (BOTH registrations), hooks/narration-meter.js, hooks/subagent-brief.js (report discipline is narration discipline), plus output-styles/hush.md as the activation half. Voices (pick-style, craft-style) and Draft (hush-compress) are OUT of scope - already opt-in by command. HUSH_NOTE context injection stays CORE: it is Core explaining its own rewrite, not narration discipline. (2) Required end state: two independent capability switches, both DEFAULT ON, plus the unchanged master. HUSH_DISABLE=1 still kills everything (162 literal disable - do not weaken it; tests/disable_conformance.test.js must stay green unchanged). Quiet off => silence-nudge, narration-meter, subagent-brief emit nothing and write nothing, while Core compression, sidecars, manifest, and both compaction hooks keep working. title: hush evidence: add adversarial transform and recovery evaluation
why: Happy-path tests do not adequately challenge metadata preservation, deletion deltas, failure placement, cleanup, recovery, or semantic drift.
what: Build a property and fixture suite for structured metadata, deletion and replacement deltas, early and late causal errors, exit signals, binary and huge output, sidecar failure and cleanup, repeated compaction, disable conformance, style rollback, and semantic document drift. notes:
Derived from docs/hush/research/hush-product-contract-and-remediation-2026-07-27.md.
2026-07-29 2026-07-29 Wave F dispatch for 174 (SS4 says 'sound as written' - no touch-list corrections; this note adds orchestrator ground truth so the coder does not rebuild what Waves A-E already pinned). GOAL, two halves. (A) An ADVERSARIAL/PROPERTY evidence layer that asserts the contract's 8 product invariants over GENERATED inputs, not hand-picked fixtures. The invariants, verbatim from docs/hush/research/hush-product-contract-and-remediation-2026-07-27.md:220-249: (1) a lossy transform without a retrievable full original is rejected; (2) a structured transform preserves every field or does not run; (3) a transform that is not smaller is rejected; (4) a user-requested range read passes verbatim; (5) a disabled hush produces no rewritten input, output, instruction, or state; (6) a missing sidecar is reported as missing, rerunning is an option and never a claim of equivalent regeneration; (7) a failure remains a failure to the surrounding execution layer unless the user explicitly selected the invasive compatibility mode; (8) statistics may report a negative outcome. (B) The entry's own requirement: ORIGINAL-OUTPUT FALLBACK WHENEVER AN INVARIANT FAILS - a runtime guard, not only a test. 164's deliver() already drops a lossy rewrite that has no recovery location and lets the original stand; generalize that one home so every invariant a transform can violate is checked there and a failed check ships the original untouched. Do not scatter per-transform guards (root-cause discipline: one fix in the shared function, not a guard in every caller). INVENTORY FIRST, THEN ADD ONLY WHAT IS MISSING. Waves A-E already committed conformance for most of the entry's named list: structured metadata + wrapper siblings and deletion/replacement deltas (163), early/late causal errors + exit signals + native-by-default + real-shell trailers (166), sidecar failure/storage-failure fallback + session cleanup (165), repeated compaction + re-arm (168), disable conformance (162, tests/disable_conformance.test.js), surface conformance (169, tests/surface_conformance.test.js), style rollback (172, tests/activate_style.test.js), semantic document drift (171, tests/verify_compression.test.js). Read those files first, write down what each already proves, and put in your report a table of 'already covered' vs 'newly covered' so the reviewer can check you added evidence rather than duplicated it. NEW GROUND 174 MUST BREAK: (a) seeded property/fuzz generation over compress() and the delta renderer - generated line mixes, cap boundaries, signal/failure/traceback vocabulary at every position, wrapper shapes, shrink/grow/replace delta shapes - asserting the invariants above hold for EVERY generated case; (b) BINARY AND HUGE OUTPUT, which nothing covers today: NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8, lone surrogates, CRLF/CR-only, ANSI-heavy, a single line of several MB, and a bounded huge payload (pick a ceiling that keeps the suite fast, state it in a comment, and say why in the report); (c) the contract's own release test at :263-267 - execute EVERY hook REGISTERED IN hooks.json with disable enabled and assert no stdout, no additionalContext, no updated input/output, and no file creation, with the hook list DERIVED FROM hooks.json rather than hand-listed, so a hook registered later cannot escape the matrix (the existing conformance files hard-code their payload lists - this is the future-proofing they lack); (d) adversarial style rollback: interrupted activation, an unwritable slot, a second activation over a half-finished one; (e) adversarial semantic drift: a corpus of drift shapes the verifier must catch, plus the shapes 171 pinned as mechanically unverifiable by design - pin the documented ceiling so it cannot silently widen. SEED LIST OF KNOWN NARROW EDGES (from Waves C/D/E non-blocking notes; use them as adversarial inputs): FAILURE_RERUN_NOTE fires on an all-kept over-cap failing run (omitted 0); repeated identical keep lines no longer fold; a traceback frame's source-echo line drops; FAILURE_RE misses 'errored'; Grep files_with_matches/count responses and content-less Reads produce no manifest record; a not-smaller-rejected grep rewrite orphans its already-written sidecar, which precompact then lists as backing a view that never shipped; claimSessionNote embeds the RAW session_id so a traversal-shaped id would create a zero-byte file outside tmpdir; a live session idle 24h can lose its sidecar namespace to another session's sweep; recoveryBytesAtMost is an upper bound. RULE FOR THESE: where current behavior is correct-but-narrow, PIN IT with a test and move on. Where a property test finds a REAL invariant violation, the fallback guard in (B) is the fix - ship the original - and every such finding gets its own paragraph in your report. Do NOT fix the listed candidates as features; they need their own roadmap entries and the user's go. DETERMINISM IS MANDATORY: seeded PRNG only, the seed printed in the failure message, no Math.random(), no wall-clock in an assertion - a flaky suite is worse than no suite. title: hush evidence: segment benchmarks and publish auditable run records
why: Aggregate benchmark wins hide workload variance and are difficult to reproduce without randomized runs, distributions, and inspectable result records.
what: Segment evaluation by noisy build and test output, ordinary coding, debugging failures, search-heavy work, and durable-document editing. Randomize order, repeat runs, report distributions and regressions, add Core-only and Quiet ablations, retain sanitized immutable run records, and generate public claims and charts from those records.

title: hush release: enforce explicit alpha exit gates
why: Without a release gate tied to trust, recovery, evidence, and truthful claims, Hush can accumulate features while its core product contract remains unproven.
what: Encode a pre-1.0 readiness checklist and executable gate covering total disable, schema and delta correctness, native failure semantics, recoverable elision, session cleanup, compaction continuity, truthful activity metrics, optional-surface isolation, adversarial evaluation, segmented benchmark evidence, and synchronized public claims.

2026-07-29 2026-07-29 Wave F dispatch for 176 (SS4 says 'sound as written'). GOAL: turn the contract's 1.0 readiness definition into an EXECUTABLE gate - a script that runs the checks and reports, per point, met or not met with the evidence it used, exiting non-zero if any point fails. A checkbox a human ticks is not a gate. THE TEN POINTS, verbatim from docs/hush/research/hush-product-contract-and-remediation-2026-07-27.md:590-603: (1) Disable means no hush behavior. (2) Every lossy view is recoverable until its disclosed expiry. (3) Structured transforms preserve all metadata. (4) Deletions and failures cannot be silently hidden. (5) Sidecars have a documented lifecycle. (6) Statistics distinguish observation from estimation. (7) Core, Quiet, Voices, and Draft have separate contracts. (8) Public claims match workload-segment evidence. (9) Configuration and stock-style recovery are stable across updates. (10) The benchmark suite reports uncertainty and publishes auditable run data. MAP EACH POINT TO A REAL CHECK, and name in the gate's own output WHICH evidence satisfied it. Most of 1-7 and 9 are already provable from committed tests and code (162/169 disable and surface conformance, 163/164 recovery metadata and structured preservation, 166 failure semantics, 165 sidecar lifecycle, 170 statistics, 172 style recovery, 174 the adversarial layer) - a check may run a named test file, assert a named invariant holds in source, or assert an artifact exists, but it must ACTUALLY EXECUTE something, not merely assert a file is present when the file's content is the claim. Points 8 and 10 depend on entry 175's segmented benchmark records, and NO PAID BATCH RUNS IN THIS WAVE - so those checks will legitimately report NOT MET, naming exactly what is missing. That is the correct outcome and the most useful thing the gate does this wave: do not fake them, do not skip them, and do not let a not-met point pass as a warning. VERIFY THE GATE ITSELF: tests that a deliberately broken fixture makes the corresponding point FAIL. A gate that cannot fail proves nothing - state your evidence that each check is falsifiable (how many points flip when you break the thing they check). Reuse the existing suite rather than reimplementing its assertions (YAGNI); the gate orchestrates evidence, it is not a second test suite. NO NEW DEPENDENCIES. SPEED: the gate is run by hand at a release boundary, so it may be slower than the unit suite, but say how long it takes. HOMES: the checklist's canonical home is the gate script itself, each point named in code beside the check that proves it. CONTRIBUTING.md may gain a short 'how to run the readiness gate' line IF it fits that file's existing shape. hush/README.md: the public-docs rule binds (current user-visible behavior only, no methodology, no roadmap, no history) - a pre-1.0 checklist is roadmap-shaped and does NOT belong there; touch README only if a current claim became literally false. CHANGELOG: a line only if user-visible behavior changed - a developer gate script usually earns none. planned_touches names docs/hush/research/hush-product-contract-and-remediation-2026-07-27.md, which lives in the PARENT repo and is the orchestrator's to edit: REPORT what you would change there, never edit it, and never edit ROADMAP.jsonl or the parent marketplace.json. title: Add the staleness resolver and the notes pull command
why: A quoted lesson with no freshness signal is the exact harm this feature exists to fix, so every served record resolves its anchor first, and every failure resolves to unknown rather than fresh.
what: Build plan task 5, spec section 'Staleness resolver'. New scripts/note-staleness.js, running only for records already selected for serving. Per record: resolve the sha (commit-kind uses the recorded sha, entry-kind uses the newest trailer sha that passes the ancestry check, and a commit-kind sha that fails existence falls back to trailer resolution because a rebase splits sha from trailer); rev-parse for existence; merge-base --is-ancestor for the history line; then `git diff --name-only -z` with the pathspecs DE-PREFIXED to scope-relative when the scope is a submodule, or submodule diffs match nothing and read fresh forever. No -M: without it a renamed anchor reports as deleted, which is the correct changed signal here. Finally existsSync per stored path; all absent means suppress plus an aggregated doctor info. Add `roadmap.js notes [--paths ...] [--area <prefix>]` with the R2 caps: at most 10 areas on an unfiltered call, a counted overflow line, and a total git-call ceiling around 30 beyond which it serves anchors only. title: Stop acquireLock leaving an empty lock directory behind forever
why: Nothing ever removes the per-project lock directory itself, so every temp project a test builds orphans one — the operator machine currently holds over 150,000 empty foreman-roadmap-*.lock directories in the system temp folder.
what: scripts/roadmap-lock.js acquireLock creates one <tmpdir>/foreman-roadmap-<hash>.lock directory per project root and only ever removes the claim directories inside it, never the container. Give the lock a release path that removes the directory when the last claim leaves, or have the test helper tear its own down; measure first which is the real source, since a production project legitimately keeps its lock directory between runs and a test fixture does not. Two related blind spots found in the same review: removeAbandonedClaim only walks claimDirectories(), which filters on the claim- prefix, so a staging- directory orphaned by a hard kill between mkdirSync and renameSync is never swept; and tests/roadmap_lock.test.js:44 activeClaims filters on the same prefix, so a future regression that did leak staging directories would pass assert.deepEqual(activeClaims(lockPath), []). Widen both filters in the same change. Verification: Run: node --test foreman/tests/roadmap_lock.test.js  Expected: green, with a new case asserting the lock directory does not survive a fixture teardown.
notes:
Raised 2026-08-18 by the adversarial review of the Tier 1-2 build. Pre-existing, unrelated to entry 230 fix, which was the staging-name race in publishClaim. Reviewer sampled 3000 live lock directories after a full suite run plus a 50-iteration loop and found zero leaked staging- entries, so the staging half is a hardening, not an observed failure; the container-directory leak is observed and large.
2026-08-18 Measured first as the entry asked: 154,039 lock containers on the operator machine, 154,032 of them empty. The container was the leak, not the claims, so the fix is in releaseLock (rmdir, which refuses a non-empty directory and so cannot race a contender) rather than in a test teardown. publishClaim retries once on ENOENT for the window that opens. Staging sweep and the widened test filter ride along. 20 consecutive green runs of the lock suite; the 154,032 empty directories were removed.

title: hush: the shell sidecar guard makes big passing output bigger, not smaller
why: maybeSidecar refuses a sidecar for any non-failing shell output at or above HUSH_SIDECAR_SHELL_MAX (28,000 chars), on the theory that the host may already have cut it. That is exactly the size where Claude Code persists the result to a file and hands the model a 2KB preview. So hush falls through to the inline cap, which cannot shrink an output whose lines all match SIGNAL_RE, ships something nearly as big, and the host persists it anyway. The model then Reads the host's parked file and the whole artifact enters context a second time. Measured across batches rm254 and rm254b, 16 runs per arm each: persisted-output hits hush 23 vs baseline 9, and chase calls (a Read or Get-Content of the host's tool-results file) hush 16 vs baseline 1, caveman 5, ste 2, adhd 1, concise 0. Conditional on hitting a persisted output hush chases 70% of the time against baseline's 11%. It shows up on feature-drift, incident-forensics and repo-sweep.
what: Free probe on the real feature-drift replay output, 54,484 chars: today hush returns 45,035 chars (-17%, decision action shell-guard-skip, sidecarPath null) because 226 rows carry the word `critical` as a PRIORITY VALUE and SIGNAL_RE preserves every one. With the guard out of the way the same input returns 3,491 chars (-94%) and the digest tail still carries `dropped: 0   route() errors: 0`, the exact line the model was chasing. Proposed fix: drop the `partial && !failed` bail in maybeSidecar so a large passing shell output gets the recovery copy too. `partial` keeps governing the HEADER only, which already says `was saved to <path> as hush received it` instead of `in full` -- the same honest wording the failing-run branch has always used. Getting hush's own output under the host's threshold is what removes the competing pointer, because the host then never persists at all. Needs: unit coverage that a large passing shell output now writes a sidecar and keeps the as-hush-received wording, that a host-truncated input still never claims `in full`, and a re-measure of the chase counts.

title: Find out why razor's build ledger never speaks in a headless session
why: razor/hooks/build-ledger.js is the one shipped mechanism never observed working in any measurement. what: Determine whether build-ledger.js runs at all under `claude -p` and, if it does, where its output goes. Leading hypothesis: a Stop hook's additionalContext on the LAST turn of a headless run has no following turn to be delivered into, so the question may be composed and discarded. Test that first by instrumenting whether build-ledger.js's process runs at all (e.g. a spy hook alongside it, the way docs/razor/research/scripts/razor-fanout-probe.js proves SubagentStart fires). Attempts to replay build-ledger.js by hand against a finished cell workspace produced no state file and no output, so a synthetic stdin payload is NOT a working reproduction — find the real input shape first. It ran, crossed its threshold, set ledger.fired, emitted its envelope, the host delivered it and the model answered it in 4 of 4 razor cells and 0 of 4 baselines. The premise was a double instrument defect in docs/razor/research/scripts/razor-ledger-probe.js. (1) State channel: the probe read [stateDir, os.tmpdir()], but Claude Code OVERWRITES CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA in every plugin hook env (claude.exe 2.1.251 hook-spawn env builder), so harness.js:97-108 resolved to ~/.claude/plugins/data/razor-inline/ — a third dir nobody searched; all four cells have a state file there with ledger.fired true and a baseSha equal to the cell git HEAD, which also REFUTES the SessionStart-baseline hypothesis.
